analysis.title: The AI scare trade is back
key_insights: Risk appetite turned fragile again on 21 Oct 2026. Brent is at $111/bbl after fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia, and the AI scare trade returned after Meta signalled higher capex.
Asia sold off: Hang Seng -3%, Kospi -3.4%, Hang Seng Tech -5%, MSCI Asia Pacific -1.5%+, TSMC -1.5%, Samsung and SK Hynix each down 4%+. China's CSI 300 is in a bear market, down 20% from its peak.
French stress is rising. The 10Y OAT yield closed at 5% for the first time since 2002, and the OAT-Bund spread is near 160bps. The 10Y OAT yield is nearly 100bps above the Spanish Bono yield.
Stress is spilling into Italy. The 10Y BTP-Bund spread closed at 115bps, below the early-October peak of 120bps, which suggests tension is mostly concentrated in OATs.
Haven flows are going to Treasuries and the yen. The 10Y UST yield is moving back towards 5.08%, and USD/JPY fell to 157.20 from 158.08. The move is amplified on EUR/JPY.
ECB hike expectations rose. The market prices nearly three 25bp hikes by the end of 2027, and the 10Y Bund traded in a 3.40%-3.45% range.

Oil recovered from Tuesday's refuted Iran-US deal headlines, then dropped on news that Putin agreed to resume US-mediated Ukraine talks as early as next month. Natixis calls this relatively neutral for crude but more bearish for diesel.
European gasoil (M1) cracks fell 5.6% to $76/bbl, still highly elevated by pre-war standards. TTF rose 1.4% near the close to EUR86.2/MWh.
UK September CPI surprised to the upside, reinforcing Natixis's call for a November BoE rate hike. UK Autumn Budget is due next week.
US equities rose for a third straight day (S&P 500 +0.6%, Nasdaq 100 +1.1%), led by SpaceX and Super Micro. S&P 500 ETFs slipped after hours on mixed Tesla and Meta results.
Meta Q3-26 beat on revenue and EPS and guided Q4 revenue above consensus. It also announced a new class of non-voting shares to fund AI spending, and shares rose 3.2% after hours.

Tesla Q3-26 beat on adjusted EPS but cut FY2026 capex guidance by $5bn to $20bn. Natixis says the cut likely sends a negative signal to investors focused on AI and robotics, and shares fell 3% after hours.
Carrefour fell a record amount after warning that social unrest in France would hit earnings, and autos underperformed in Europe.
Natixis credit trade idea: buy SocGen 6% call 08/31 AT1 and sell Eurobank 6.625% call 05/31 AT1.

market_movers.rationale: Q3-26 revenue of $64.6bn beat consensus by $1.3bn and grew 26% YoY. Q4 revenue guidance of $73-76bn is above the $73.5bn forecast. Shares rose 3.2% after hours.
Adjusted EPS of $0.24 beat the $0.20 estimate, but FY2026 capex guidance was cut by $5bn to $20bn. Natixis says this likely sends a negative signal. Shares fell 3% after hours.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3-26 (reported): revenue $64.6bn vs consensus about $63.3bn (beat by $1.3bn), up 26% YoY. EPS $3.83 reported vs $3.57 consensus estimate. 2026 capex outlook narrowed to $135-145bn from $130-145bn. Q4 revenue guidance $73-76bn vs $73.5bn consensus forecast.

Tesla Q3-26 (reported): adjusted EPS $0.24 vs $0.20 consensus estimate. Gross margin 19.6%, up 1.6pp YoY, on flat sales. Free cash flow $1.5bn, a $3bn sequential improvement. FY2026 capex guidance cut by $5bn to $20bn.
Thales (reported through 30 Sep 2026): order intake EUR19.1bn, up 15% organically. Revenue EUR16.4bn, up 8.1%. The group expects growth close to or above the upper end of its guidance range.
Iberdrola 9M-26 results (reported) beat expectations, and management raised 2026 net profit guidance.
Carrefour warned that social unrest in France would hit earnings, and the stock fell a record amount.
